about: Fidelity is one of the family labels of Nick Goldschmidt, the New Zealand-born winemaker who moved to Sonoma in 1989, ran the cellar at Simi and later oversaw winemaking for Allied Domecq and Beam Estates. He now directs projects on several continents from his base in Alexander Valley, and his guiding idea is transparency: one vintage, one vineyard, one variety, so the guest knows exactly what is in the bottle.

The Railyard is a small old vineyard near Geyserville at the northern end of Alexander Valley, first planted in the late 1800s, which Wine Spectator singled out when Nick first bottled it. Old Zinfandel vines like these give small crops of concentrated fruit, and Alexander Valley’s warm days and cool river-influenced nights let it ripen fully while keeping freshness. In earlier vintages Nick aged the wine about 16 months in mostly seasoned French oak so the fruit stays in front.

Critics describe the 2023 as rich yet balanced: blackberry, plum, raspberry and fresh cherry, licorice, cracked pepper and a touch of mocha, with smooth, rounded tannins. Look too for blackberry jam, Asian spice and a long, supple finish. Both James Suckling and Wine Spectator scored the 2023 at 92 points, the same mark Wine Spectator gave the 2018 Railyard, which says a good deal for a wine sealed under a simple screw cap and priced for everyday drinking.
